hints: Combine fractions on the LHS over $(1 + \cos\theta)(1 - \cos\theta) = 1 - \cos^2\theta = \sin^2\theta$.
walkthrough:
Combine the two terms on the LHS over their common denominator:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\tan\theta(1 - \cos\theta) + \tan\theta(1 + \cos\theta)}{(1 + \cos\theta)(1 - \cos\theta)}$$

Simplify the denominator using the Pythagorean identity $1 - \cos^2\theta = \sin^2\theta$:
$$\text{Denominator} = 1 - \cos^2\theta = \sin^2\theta$$

Substitute $\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ and cancel a factor of $\sin\theta$:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{2\left(\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\right)}{\sin^2\theta} = \frac{2\sin\theta}{\cos\theta\sin^2\theta} = \frac{2}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}$$

hints: Find both angles in degrees for $0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Substitute the identity into the given trigonometric equation:
$$\frac{2}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} = \frac{6}{\tan\theta} = \frac{6\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}$$

Take square roots to find both positive and negative values:
$$\cos\theta = \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \approx \pm 0.57735$$
